limit/recap: On the bowl a x squared, every step multiplies x by one minus two a eta. With a at one and a learning rate of zero point eight, that is minus zero point six, and x zigzags in.
limit/line: Plot the factor against eta. It starts at one and falls in a straight line as eta grows.
limit/half: At eta equals one over two a, it is zero: a single step lands right on the minimum.
limit/edge: At one over a, it reaches minus one, and x bounces between two points forever. Any larger, and it blows up.
limit/solve: Why one over a? Set the factor to minus one: one minus two a eta equals minus one. Then two a eta is two, and eta is one over a.
limit/steep: A steeper bowl, a bigger a, makes the line fall faster, so it reaches minus one sooner: at a half, when a is two. The largest learning rate that does not diverge, written eta max, is one over a.
slide/shift: Now slide the bowl so its bottom sits at three: f of x equals a times x minus three, squared. Each slope is the old one at the same distance from the bottom, so the gradient is two a, times x minus three.
slide/dist: From x equals four, with eta at zero point three, the distance x minus three goes one, zero point four, zero point one six: the same factor, one minus two a eta, every step. Sliding the bowl moves the minimum, and nothing else: the limit is still one over a.
try/p1: Try one: f of x is four times x minus three, squared. What is the largest eta that does not diverge?
try/a1: Sliding moves only the minimum, so a is still four. Set the factor to minus one: one minus eight eta is minus one, so eight eta is two, and eta is zero point two five.
try/p2: Which eta lands on the minimum in a single step?
try/a2: Set the factor to zero instead: one minus eight eta is zero, so eight eta is one, and eta is one eighth, zero point one two five.
try/p3: And what does x do with eta at zero point two? The factor is one minus eight times zero point two: minus zero point six, between minus one and zero. x zigzags in.
